analysis.convergence_comparison: At epoch 30, coupling_512 (loss=245.0) shows only 1.8% improvement over baseline_256 (loss=249.4). The larger model converges to essentially the same loss despite 4x more parameters.
analysis.training_speed: coupling_512 takes 2x longer per epoch (24.8s vs 12.5s) due to 4x more parameters. The marginal loss improvement does not justify the 2x training cost.
analysis.expected_primary_score: Based on the loss trajectory, coupling_512 would likely achieve Primary ~0.65-0.67 at epoch 40, similar to baseline_256 (0.6634).
analysis.verdict: Larger coupling dimension (512) does NOT provide meaningful improvement. The 256-dim bottleneck is NOT the limiting factor. The problem is likely in the architecture design (encoder/decoder structure) or the training approach, not in the coupling capacity.
